evidence.note: Early stated intent to inspect all crates then build leaf-first (common/storage before scheduler/controllers); dependency-aware ordering declared, though not a written per-crate milestone plan for all ten crates.
Treated common+storage as a milestone with an explicit done-check ('common/storage targeted tests now pass') before moving to scheduler/controller-manager — matches the level-5 per-crate gate.
Scheduler gated as green (19/19) before focusing on controller-manager runtime; layering each crate on the prior being green.

Decomposed the large controller-manager crate into per-controller sub-milestones (VPA, volume-snapshot, volume-expansion, TTL, StatefulSet, ServiceAccount, Service, ResourceQuota, ReplicaSet), each with a 'focused test passes' exit criterion and a full-suite rerun to select the next cluster — anchor-8 sub-milestone structure plus failure-cluster-driven re-ordering.

After CM/scheduler green, moved to full workspace and only then hit kubelet/api-server/etc. as an undifferentiated batch of compile errors with no milestone structure or exit criteria; these downstream crates were never sequenced or finished, keeping it below anchor 8.

reasoning: The agent decisively exceeds anchor 5: it followed a dependency-aware leaf-first order (common→storage→scheduler→controller-manager→workspace) with per-crate 'compiles + tests pass' gates, and it exhibited genuine anchor-8 behavior by decomposing the large controller-manager crate into independently verifiable per-controller units, each with a crisp done-check, gating the full suite green after each, and re-ordering by test-failure clusters. It falls short of a full 8/10 because there was no explicit up-front milestone plan covering all ten crates with exit criteria, high-risk crates (api-server) were not isolated early, and the entire lower tier (api-server, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) was handled as one unstructured compile-error push at the end. That places it solidly between anchors 5 and 8, i.e. a 7.
